text:
anya: Heads-up: onboarding Noctua7B (llama-ish) and hitting a weird "token stitch" during vocab+rotary conversion. Short repro below — anyone seen this pattern? :thinking:

devon: not exactly that name. show the converter flags and a tiny failing example?

anya: we ran: `python convert.py --from=llama --to=redwood --vocab-map=legacy-map.json --rotary=perhead-wrap --merge-sentinels=true`
example: prompt `The cat sat on the` then next-token logits spike and an unexpected token appears mid-output.

sam: can you paste token ids for the prefix that triggers the spike?

anya: ids: [43, 129, 78, 9, 1423] — 1423 should have been two subtokens [1423, 2] under legacy-map, but converter produced a single id (merged).

maria: merging subtokens will change the token index stream. Rotary sin/cos are tied to token positions per head, so merging could shift per-head phase; plus kv cache indexing expects stable token segmentation.

devon: does this show up in the kv-cache offsets during warmup?

anya: yes. traced a warmup run with kvcache enabled:
```
step=10 kv_index_expected=100 kv_index_actual=102
```
consistent +2 offset after the merged token.

triage-bot: nightly conversion sweep completed. Noctua7B: PPL delta +3.0 vs baseline on short-context set; stitch-suite fail rate 4.9%. Artifacts: /runs/noctua/1812/convert-01

sam: will run quant sensitivity sweep (FP16 -> int8 -> int4). do we suspect quant multiplies the effect?

maria: likely — quantized kernels can increase logit jitter, which might amplify a transient caused by mis-indexed rotary.

devon: quick mitigation?

anya: temporary fix: expand merged tokens back to original subtokens during conversion (simple demerge table). pseudo: `if tid in merge_tbl: out.extend(merge_tbl[tid])` — restores segmentation and eliminates the offset leak in my local tests. Ugly but effective.

sam: add that demerge as an optional conversion pass and I'll include it in the int4 sweep tonight.

maria: long-term we should: (1) make converter canonicalize segmentation semantics (no silent merges) and (2) make rotary indexing resilient to variable token grouping (derive phase from absolute subtoken positions). File a ticket?

devon: filing ML-2468 to cover canonical converter behavior + rotary robustness. assign to infra/eng-ml; priority P1 if quant sweep shows amplification.

anya: added a tiny failing case and sample model slices to the ticket. also pushed a quick branch `fix/noctua-demerge` with the demerge table and a unit test that asserts kv offsets stable for first 16 warmup steps. PR: https://redwood/pull/1299

sam: ran FP16 vs int4 on my laptop VM against the demerge branch: stitch pass rate with FP16=98.7%, int4=89.3% (without demerge int4 was 72.1%). uploading full logs to the run artifacts.

maria: good data. suggests quant amplifies but demerge closes most of the gap. we still need converter canonicalization to avoid shipping fragile maps.

devon: agreed. I'll take ML-2468. in parallel we should scan existing legacy vocab maps for any with merge-sentinels=true and mark them for rebuild. low-effort script: grep + list -> rebuild queue.

anya: ran a quick grep: ~37 legacy maps flagged. added to ML-2468 checklist.

triage-bot: ML-2468 created and assigned to dev:devon; reporter:anya; priority:high.

sam: follow-up: I'll attach the int4 cross-entropy deltas and stitch-suite diffs to the ticket tomorrow AM.

maria: can someone add a small converter unit test matrix: (merge true/false) x (kvcache on/off) x (rotary modes) -> assert kv offsets and logits within tolerance for N seeds. that would catch regressions early.

anya: added test matrix to the PR description. will iterate on coverage.

devon: thanks. once the PR lands we'll roll it to the onboarding harness and re-run full Noctua sweep.

anya: leaving a small obf log snippet from the failing run:
```
prefix tokens: [43,129,78,9,1423]
logits step5: [0.1,-0.9,2.4,8.9,12.0]  # spike at merged token
post-normalize: downstream tokens realign after 2 steps
```

sam: noted — I'll attach the normalized cross-ent and stitch traces to the PR. :thumbsup:

maria: solid plan. thanks everyone. keeping this in the onboarding checklist until ML-2468 is resolved. :white_check_mark:
